title: Service-to-Service Authentication
description: Learn to authenticate service-to-service communication in microservices.

data.text: In microservices, internal services must authenticate each other to prevent unauthorized access. Google, Amazon, and Netflix all use mTLS and service identities to ensure that only authorized services can communicate.

Service-to-service authentication ensures that only legitimate services can call each other. Common patterns include mTLS, API keys, JWT with service claims, and service meshes like Istio that handle authentication automatically.

mTLS extends TLS by requiring both client and server to present certificates. This provides strong authentication: the server verifies the client's certificate, and the client verifies the server's certificate. Service meshes like Istio automate mTLS for microservices.

data.title: Service-to-Service Auth Approaches
items: Service JWT: JWTs with service-specific claims
API keys: Shared secrets between services (less secure)
Service mesh: Istio/Linkerd automate mTLS and authz
Network policies: Kubernetes NetworkPolicies restrict traffic

data.title: Istio mTLS
data.text: Istio, used by Google and IBM, provides automatic mTLS between services. It issues certificates to each service and handles rotation, eliminating the need for manual certificate management.

data.title: Example: mTLS with Istio
data.content: Enable mTLS in Istio for a namespace.
data.code:
# Enable strict mTLS for all services in the namespace
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
  namespace: production
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT
---
# Allow specific service to communicate without mTLS
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: DestinationRule
metadata:
  name: legacy-service
  namespace: production
spec:
  host: legacy-service
  trafficPolicy:
    tls:
      mode: DISABLE

data.caption: mTLS between services
data.definition:
graph LR
    S1[Service A] -->|mTLS| S2[Service B]
    S1 -->|Certificate| C1[Client Cert]
    S2 -->|Certificate| C2[Server Cert]
    C1 -->|Verify| S2
    C2 -->|Verify| S1

items.question: What is the difference between mTLS and TLS?
items.answer: TLS authenticates only the server. mTLS authenticates both client and server, providing mutual authentication.

items.question: Is mTLS hard to implement?
items.answer: Manually, yes. With a service mesh like Istio, it is trivial. The mesh handles certificate issuance, rotation, and validation automatically.

items.question: What if I cannot use a service mesh?
items.answer: Use JWT with service claims or implement certificate management with tools like Vault. Kubernetes cert-manager can automate certificate issuance.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Internal services must authenticate each other
mTLS provides the strongest service-to-service authentication
Service meshes automate mTLS and certificate management
Never trust internal traffic by default
data.takeaway: Implement mTLS or equivalent for all service-to-service communication.
